newsitem.title: USA: USDA -- CIS, Baltics meat imports seen robust.
newsitem.headline: USDA -- CIS, Baltics meat imports seen robust.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Tuesday predicted meat imports into the former Soviet Union would remain robust but did not forsee a rebound in grain sales.

In an outlook report, USDA's Economic Research Service pegged 1997 total meat imports into the region at near last year's record two million tonnes, citing a continued lack of competitiveness by domestic producers.
Net grain imports in the region in 1997/98 were projected at a record low of under four million tonnes. By comparision, in the 1980's, imports ran over 30 million tonnes a year.
"The region is not expected to return to the large grain imports of the pre-reform period, or to become a major grain exporter," the report said.
"Net grain imports in 2005 are projected at 2-3 million tonnes, primarily wheat, while in certain years there could be small net exports of coarse grains," it continued.
The USDA report forecast total U.S. agricultural sales to the area would grow over 10 percent from a year earlier in fiscal 1997, as exports of meat and other consumer-ready products rise.
Poultry meat is the single largest U.S export to the region with sales of about $1 billion in calendar year 1996.
